mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the next month reduces discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings for equities and thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises continuously for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of observed rising-rate periods, or the 20-day IC is >0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening labor market and reduced business confidence, which depresses equity valuations and drives negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by >5% while INDPRO falls by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in >70% of similar labor market weakness events, or interaction index (IC) >0.04.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer spending (HOUST) above 1% of GDP in a month of falling unemployment (UNRATE < 4%) indicates strong demand that outpaces supply, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% while UNRATE falls below 4% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative in >40% of such demand spikes, or interaction index < -0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 3% in two consecutive months suggests supply-side weakness that persists into the next quarter, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over a 60-day horizon as investors price in recovery.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative in >60% of observed INDPRO contractions.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, the central bank's policy shift toward easing is expected to boost risk appetite, yielding positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero in 95% of such events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% coinciding with a rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market that pressures inflation and weighs on equity valuations, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% while PAYEMS increases by >10,000 in a month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >50% of such labor tightness episodes, or interaction index >0.07.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in retail activity (HOUST) exceeding 4% in a period of stable inflation (CPIAUCSL < 0.2%) indicates strong demand that anticipates higher corporate profits, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >4% while CPIAUCSL remains below 0.2%
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative in >30% of such demand spikes, or interaction index < -0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month cumulative change in S&P 500 total returns is positive while the 12-month change in GDP (not in the catalog) is negative, the macroeconomic divergence suggests a structural shift favoring equities over real activity, producing positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows negative 12-month cumulative return while SPX shows positive 12-month cumulative return
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly different from zero in 80% of such divergence events (p > 0.15).
